headline: The ARMOR-X body, connected directly over its own USB port, enumerates as the SAME vendor HID identity as the F20 (413d:2106 Zikway 'HID zk', byte-identical 29-byte report descriptor, no serial) and is COMPLETELY SILENT: zero payload-bearing frames, and a physical A-button press produced no USB traffic at all. So the vendor FF7A personality is a configuration/diagnostic channel, not an input channel.

direct_enumeration.port: bus 1 port 1-7 (same port the F20 used)
direct_enumeration.endpoints: 0x83 IN interrupt 64 B bInterval 8; 0x03 OUT interrupt 64 B bInterval 8
direct_enumeration.descriptor_vs_f20: IDENTICAL - byte-for-byte equal to the F20 vendor descriptor frozen in the previous run

traffic.button_test: operator ACK press_a_direct at 15:24:09 (t~290 s): A pressed twice - NO traffic of any kind appeared on the body's interface
traffic.conclusion: silent at rest and silent under input; the device-side vendor interface does not carry controller state

back_to_vendor: 20440.507 device 9 413d:2106 vendor HID again, clean single re-enumeration
direct_body: 20796.735 device 10 413d:2106 after the operator connected the ARMOR-X body directly (ACK connect_armorx_direct 15:21:22)
identity_cycle_confirmed.reading: the receiver round-trips vendor -> Xbox -> vendor, and the body on its own USB presents the vendor identity, so identity is driven by whether a wireless/host controller session is active

disambiguation: The direct device was indistinguishable from the F20 by USB evidence alone (same VID/PID, bcdDevice, strings, descriptor hash, endpoints, and no serial), so I ran a one-shot popup asking the operator which unit was physically connected; the answer was ARMOR-X PRO body (ack identify_current_device, 15:23:15). Without that answer this conclusion could not have been drawn from the wire.
architecture_implication: Xbox controller -> ARMOR-X internal USB HOST -> normalized state is still the leading model, and it is now supported by firmware strings rather than only caller placement: the trio reference the diagnostic 'usbh_socket_en = %d, m_xbox_enum_step= %d, usbh_gamepad_ready= %d, usbh_gamepadp = %p', which names a USB-host socket enable, an XBOX ENUMERATION STEP variable and the gamepad pointer. The body's own device-mode USB is not that path - it is silent.
not_proven: the trio's report field offsets (no live payload exists to match against on the device-side interface)
that the Xbox input path reaches state+0x1d4 (architecture supported, path not traced)
the normalized state field names beyond the previously proven mask/axes/LT/RT layout

safety.popups: four, all ACKed and closed (remove_f20, connect_armorx_direct, identify_current_device, press_a_direct)
safety.agent_initiated_writes: none - no control requests sent, no HID output reports, no feature sets
safety.automatic_host_traffic: present and separate from agent actions: the Linux HID core submitted 12 interrupt IN and 3 interrupt OUT URBs at probe on both vendor-mode devices, and in Xbox mode the kernel/xpad generated its normal GIP initialization output (documented in the F20 artifact). None of that was agent-generated.
safety.capture: tcpdump stopped; no capture process left running
